new_findings.kind: the guard of the one silence grant reads a marked-content state that skips streams: a kept page's /Contents entry that `seen` already holds (a repeated entry, or a stream a nested form read consumed first) adds none of its BDC /OC to the page's stack, so a Do inside optional content can be granted silence. Claim contradicted: 'the nesting of BMC, BDC and EMC tracked per operator across the streams of the page' (V4-07 class: shipped claim wider than the code).
new_findings.file_line: src/flatten_purge.rs:703-705 (`if !seen.insert(*num) { continue; }`), :701 and :716-722 (marked changes only for streams read), :744 and :748 (the guard and the one grant), :771-772 (nested read shares `seen`), :791-792 (one `seen` per scope); src/show_text.rs:967-978 (content_streams_of keeps duplicates); src/canon.rs:294-336 (merge only when no segment fails). Claims: src/flatten_purge.rs:72-74, src/lib.rs:95 (redaction.flatten.purge and painted_over).
new_findings.evidence: Reasoned from the code at 12c9317, not executed. read_scope keeps ONE `seen` set per scope (created at :791, handed to every nested call at :772) and skips any stream number already in it (:703-705). For a kept page the streams are its /Contents list as written (content_streams_of, show_text.rs:967-978, no de-duplication), and the marked-content stack `marked` (:701) is changed only by streams that are read (:716-722). A stream that the page lists but that `seen` already holds therefore adds none of its BMC/BDC/EMC to the page's stack, while a viewer executes every listed stream at page level (ISO 32000 page /Contents: the streams of an array act as one concatenated stream; the clause number is NOT_INSPECTED here). Two ways in. (1) Repeated entry: kept page two /Contents [70 70 71 72] (indirect streams), 70 = `/OC /MC0 BDC` (the bytes of the case at tests/flatten_r13.rs:946), 71 = `EMC q 10 0 0 10 400 100 cm /Im1 Do Q`, 72 = a stream the strict parser rejects (so canonicalize refuses the page and leaves its four streams, canon.rs:301-305 and :328-329); page two's /Resources lists /Im1 as the region image 10 through dictionary objects only. Code: 70 pushes true (:718); the second 70 is skipped (:703-705); 71: EMC pops (:720), marked is empty, `/Im1 Do`: nearest 0, plain, `!marked.contains(&true)` (:744), plain_image(10) => silent.insert(10) (:748); 72 fails to parse (:714) => all_used (:793), 10 stays silent; 10 is live and :911 does not return it: painted_sources_kept == []. The page-level sequence is BDC(/OC) BDC(/OC) EMC Do, so the Do is inside an optional-content sequence that is still open (possibly hidden), which the lead decision and the docs (flatten_purge.rs:72-74, lib.rs:95) say is not silent. (2) A stream used elsewhere: /Contents [70 71 72 73], 70 = `/Fx Do` with /Fx a form WITHOUT /Resources whose stream is object 71 (listed in page two's /XObject), 71 = `/OC /MC0 BDC`, 72 = `q 10 0 0 10 400 100 cm /Im1 Do Q`, 73 = a rejected stream as in (1). The `Do /Fx` in 70 reads 71 as nested content first (:771-772, page false, its own fresh stack), which puts 71 into `seen`; the page's own entry 71 is then skipped, its BDC /OC never reaches the page's stack, and 72's Do is silent although the page-level sequence BDC(/OC) Do is inside optional content. This route does not depend on how a viewer treats a repeated entry: the stream is listed once and every viewer executes it at page level. Bound: both need the page left as written, i.e. canonicalize refused it (canon.rs:301-317: an unreadable or ambiguous stream, streams that do not join cleanly, operands left across streams); when it succeeds the page's streams are merged in order, duplicates included (canon.rs:300-325), and the single new stream is read correctly. A refused page keeps non-canonical or unreadable streams, so the output carries NotProven::NonCanonicalContent or UnreadableContent (sanitized_save.rs:1388-1406) and is_proven() and region_cleared() read false; painted_sources_kept (the lane's claim) is empty, and region_flattened() (sanitized_save.rs:1416-1423) does not read those two reasons (it also needs proof.structural_reasons(false) without Structure: NOT_INSPECTED for this document). Viewer behaviour for a repeated /Contents entry is UNVERIFIED (pdf.js may read a shared Stream object once). Coverage: no test lists a stream twice or shares a stream between /Contents and a form (tests/flatten_r13.rs:940-962 use distinct streams), so a mutant that never skips the page's streams survives every test read. The V4-06 class regex (notes.remediation_R18pre.v4_06) has no `seen.insert(` token, so the class listing cannot show the site. The same code stood at bcc0688 (the R18 pre-review read the stack as OK in b_adversarial_routes_checked.marked_content_nesting_across_streams without the `seen` skip); it is the guard of the one grant the lead reduced the claim to.
new_findings.remediation: Make the page scope read every listed occurrence in order: `let first = seen.insert(*num); if !first && !page { continue; }` at :703-705 (the page's streams still enter `seen`, so nested reads of the same stream stay cycle-safe and skipped; the page-level read no longer depends on what a nested read did first; the decode budget and `steps` already charge each read). Cheaper fail-closed alternative: when `page` and `seen.insert` returns false, set a scope-local `marked_unknown` and grant no further silence in that scope (a Do already recorded before the skip used an exact stack). Tests (fail on 12c9317, pass after): the two documents above expected painted_sources_kept == [10] and PaintedSourceKept among the reasons, bytes stay; controls: the same pages with the streams listed once and a closed sequence (EMC then Do) stay silent, so the repeated entry is the cause. Add the token `seen.insert(` to the V4-06 class regex and re-list.
